note: Russia: Belarusians move freely; nationals of the countries listed enter without a visa for 90, 60, 30 or 14 days (most within 90 days a calendar year or a set period, not modelled; China's and Vietnam's 30 days temporary, to 2027), but every visa-exempt visitor must first obtain an electronic travel authorisation with a QR code through the Gosuslugi app (taken as an ETA). Nationals of the e-Visa list (the EU, most of Europe and Asia's partners) apply online for 30 days, entering at the listed crossings; everyone else needs a visa, the United States, Canada, the UK and Australia among them. Read from Wikipedia's copy of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' rules. Checked on 2026-11-03 against the Consular Department's own e-visa portal and its list of the 64 states whose citizens may get the e-visa: every passport held for the e-visa is on it; so are Estonia and Latvia, which Wikipedia's copy, read before, had among the visa-free: its visa-free entries for them are for the holders of their non-citizen passports, so their citizens were moved to the e-visa. The list's other states that are also visa-free (China, Jordan, North Macedonia, Myanmar, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Vietnam) keep the visa-free entry. The e-visa's 30 days, the visa-free list and the electronic travel authorisation stand on Wikipedia's copy.
